image_description: A large, white built-in bookcase unit spanning a wall corner. The structure features multiple vertical sections with adjustable shelves filled with books of various sizes and colors. A central section includes a small cabinet door at the bottom and an open shelf above it. The top of the bookcase has a decorative cornice molding. The floor is light-colored wood.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rectangular furniture piece of considerable height, notably taller than wide.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The overall structure is clearly a tall rectangular furniture piece, significantly taller than its individual bay widths, fitting the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tall rectangular frame with horizontal divisions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bookcase exhibits a clear rectangular frame with distinct horizontal shelves dividing the space.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bilateral symmetry with open front displaying books and objects.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the individual bays have some symmetry, the overall unit is asymmetrical due to the corner configuration and varying contents/shelf heights. However, it does have an open front displaying books.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Multiple horizontal shelves spaced evenly from top to bottom.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There are multiple shelves in each vertical section. While not perfectly identical in spacing across all sections (some adjustability visible), they are generally evenly spaced within each bay.
Small holes for shelf pins are visible on the inner sides of the vertical supports, indicating adjustability.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Some models have glass doors on upper section.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: No glass doors are visible on this specific bookcase model; all shelves appear open.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Constructed from wood particleboard or metal with finished surface stained painted or laminated.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The surface appears to be painted wood or MDF, consistent with typical bookcase construction.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Front open displaying books and objects on each shelf.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: All visible shelves are open-fronted and contain books or other items.
The unit features decorative cornice molding at the top and paneling details, indicating finished surfaces and decorative elements.

artifact_observations.reasoning: Many book spines show illegible text, warped lettering, or nonsensical patterns, which is a common AI artifact when rendering detailed text on small objects.

artifact_observations.location: Top right corner where the bookcase meets the ceiling/wall
artifact_observations.reasoning: The molding and top edge of the bookcase blend slightly into the background wall/ceiling area, lacking sharp definition and realistic shadowing, suggesting minor geometric fusion.

artifact_observations.location: Vertical lines of the bookcase bays
artifact_observations.reasoning: Some vertical lines appear slightly wavy or inconsistent in parallelism, particularly in the leftmost section, indicating minor perspective warping.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the primary object classification as 'bookcase' and distinguish it from similar furniture like shelving units or cabinets.
To verify the 3D structural integrity of the shelves and frames, checking for melting or impossible geometry in the complex joinery.
To audit the boundaries between individual books and shelves, detecting any fusion or bleeding artifacts common in dense object arrangements.
To specifically analyze the legibility and coherence of text on book spines, a high-risk area for AI artifacts.

focus_areas: Legibility and consistency of text on book spines
Structural integrity of shelf supports and vertical dividers
Sharpness of boundaries between books and shelves
Geometric consistency of perspective lines in the bookcase frame
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the text on book spines; even if the classifier confirms 'bookcase', severe text gibberish can indicate low-quality generation. Check if the geometric depth auditor finds any impossible overlaps between shelves and back panels. Verify if the topology auditor detects any books merging into each other or the shelves.
